title: advisory-priors v1
description: Advisory routing priors for the Meshloop kernel (ADR 0038, amendment 2026-11-10 for #139). Routing priors only: tier hints and planning notes are deferred until a GO at #140 and are not part of v1 (a file carrying them has unknown top-level fields, which are ignored). The nodecode-meshloop cell writes the file as a proposal; it has effect only after `meshloop priors accept --file F --as <identity>` stores its bytes in the append-only promotion ledger. The kernel loader, not this schema, is the authority. Length limits here count code points; the kernel counts UTF-8 bytes. A file-level failure means no priors; an entry-level failure (including an unknown field inside an entry) ignores that entry; unknown top-level fields are ignored. Every case yields a diagnostic, never a failed command. No field carries worker output.

source.description: Optional pointers to what was folded. Display only.

priors.description: One entry per key (harness, model_ref, tier, dispatch_mode). The kernel derives pi = (successes + 1) / (attempts + 2) and passes it through the PredictiveSuccessOracle port into fused_historical_mean; the file never states pi. Entries sharing a key are all ignored (duplicate_key).

attempt_ref.description: An attempt Meshloop dispatched as subprocess, with model_passed true and a recorded check_result. `passed` is that check_result.

model_ref.description: The model recorded on the attempt rows (#134). The kernel applies #134's model_ref predicate, moved to meshloop-domain: non-empty, at most 256 bytes, no leading '-', no whitespace or control characters. `unverified` (ADR 0039) is refused.

dispatch_mode.description: Positive marker. Only subprocess attempts are evidence for #139.

attempts.description: Must equal the length of provenance and be at least the kernel's floor (5) to have effect.

successes.description: Must equal the number of provenance refs with passed = true.

provenance.description: One reference per counted attempt. The loader also refuses two refs naming the same (graph_id, task_id, attempt_id) whatever their `passed` (duplicate_provenance).
